record.name: Aged Sheng Pu Song Dynasty Tribute Tea

paragraphs.text: This is [raw pu’er](sheng:identity) from Yunnan, made in 2005 and left loose rather than pressed. Raw pu’er is never hot-air dried after the wok, so some of the leaf’s own activity survives, and that is what lets the [rough tea, or maocha](sheng:making), keep changing for years.

At twenty-one years it has passed the point where many in the trade begin to call raw pu’er [aged](sheng:ageing), though some count from ten. Without shou’s quick fermentation, all of that change has come slowly, [in storage](sheng:aging), so how and where it was kept is part of this tea’s history as much as the years are.

brewing.text: Young raw pu’er takes water a little off the boil, about 85 to 95°C, because hotter water draws out more of its bitterness; an aged one takes 95°C to boiling. A common start is about 7 grams to 100 ml and a quick rinse of a few seconds, then a first steep of ten to fifteen seconds, adding a few seconds each round. A good raw tea gives eight to ten cups or more.

notice.text: A smoother, thicker, sweeter cup with woody, herbal and camphor notes and something of dried dates or dark fruit.
